name: BACH_0164
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (100%)** · Confident · Read in turn
Single-class set, high reliability, and second-model agreement support this [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 100%, InSitu <1% | Near-certain, calibrated |
| Conformal set | {Benign} at 90% | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.997 / 76th percentile | Input looks typical |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Agrees |
| Similar cases | 4 of 5 Benign | Mostly consistent |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor-infiltrating stroma** (region 9) · ↑ invasive · Scores well below typical; lowers invasive association [F2] · Validated
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 0, 5, 8) · ↓ invasive · High score; associated with lower invasive likelihood [F3] · Validated
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (region 2) · ↓ invasive · Scarce here; small push toward invasive [F4] · Validated
- **Tumor cell fraction** (regions 1, 6, 10) · context · 89% neoplastic nuclei, top of reference set; conflicts with Benign [F7] · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Top-3 deletion beats random by 0.54 logit (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to classifier.
- **Concepts**: Effect 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0; not shown to reflect classifier. Mitoses and normal lobules (0/20) are Unreliable; disregard.

## Could be wrong if
- Sampled regions 1, 6, 10 are 89% neoplastic nuclei; if truly tumor, Benign is wrong.
- Tubule score is text-prompt only, flagged caption-inconsistent.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 1, 6, 10:** Confirm whether "neoplastic" nuclei are carcinoma or benign proliferation.
2. **Region 9:** Look for tumor-cell infiltration of the stroma.
3. **Regions 0, 5, 8:** Confirm gland formation looks benign.
